entries.value: doors are left unlocked but gates are chained
no one says a person's name on the day they die
bread is broken, never cut, at a funeral
newcomers are asked three questions before their first meal
the oldest child keeps the family tools
a bell rings once for a birth and twice for a debt
guests must bring their own cup
the river is thanked before it is crossed
arguments happen in the street, apologies in the kitchen
harvest hands are fed before the family
no work is done on the first fog of the month
every roof carries a stone from the road it faces
the dead are remembered by what they lent, not what they owned
